# RECORD

Counts or measures something as entities pass (a count, a time between arrivals, a defect, a cost) in a user-named statistic, without delaying them.

A zero-time block that updates a user-defined statistic and forwards the entity unchanged.

Statistics live on the simulation context (`ctx.user_stats`), keyed by `stat_name`, so two RECORD blocks writing to the same name share one collector -- core/schema/ rejects a same-name pair with different `kind`s at load time, before a run can hit the mismatch here.

`expr` is the increment for "count", the observed value for "tally", the new level for "time_persistent", and ignored for "time_between" (it tallies the gap since the statistic's last arrival; the first arrival records nothing).

`kind="cost"` is the one kind that builds no collector: `expr` is a MONEY amount added to the cost item `stat_name` every time an entity passes -- an ordering cost, a changeover cost, a lost-sale penalty. It joins the model's Total Cost and is itemised in the `cost_summary` frame.

Family: stats. Python builder: `m.record(...)`.

## Typical uses

Use RECORD to measure something as entities pass, without delaying them: a count of defects, the time between arrivals, a value per order, a cost. The result is a named statistic in the `user_summary` frame. To change an attribute or a variable, use [ASSIGN](assign.md).

## Behaviour and rules

The `kind` sets what is recorded. `count` adds `expr` to a running total. `tally` collects `expr` as an observation and reports its mean and spread. `time_between` records the gap since the previous arrival and ignores `expr`, and the first arrival records nothing. `time_persistent` sets a level to `expr` and reports its time average.

Two RECORD blocks with the same `stat_name` share one statistic. They must have the same `kind`, or a check reports an error. The default `expr` is 1, which makes `count` a simple counter.

The kind `cost` builds no statistic. It adds `expr`, an amount of money, to the cost item `stat_name` each time an entity passes. The item joins the total cost and the `cost_summary` frame, grouped under `category`. The warm-up clears user statistics and event costs.

## Ports

- Inputs: any number of incoming links.
- Outputs: one outgoing link.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Required | Quantity | Unit key | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `stat_name` | str | `''` | yes |  |  | Name of the user statistic; two RECORD blocks with the same name share one collector. |
| `kind` | str | `'count'` |  |  |  | "count" (running total of expr), "tally" (mean of expr), "time_between" (mean gap between arrivals), "time_persistent" (time-average level of expr) or "cost" (adds expr to a named cost item and to Total Cost). |
| `expr` | str | `'1'` |  |  |  | Expression evaluated at each arrival; ignored for kind=time_between. |
| `category` | str | `''` |  |  |  | Cost category this item is grouped under in the cost_summary frame; used by kind=cost only. |

## Statistics

Every run fills `system` and `entity_summary` (see the [KPI reference](../kpis.md)). The example below also fills:

| Frame | Columns |
|---|---|
| [`user_summary`](../kpis.md#user_summary) | `Run`, `Statistic`, `Kind`, `Count`, `Value`, `Min`, `Max`, `Std` |
| `material_flow_summary` | `Run`, `From`, `To`, `Entities` |

## Problem codes

A check of the model reports these about this block:

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `E_RECORD_KIND` | A RECORD block's kind is not a known user-statistic kind. |
| `E_RECORD_KIND_CONFLICT` | Two RECORD blocks give the same statistic different kinds. |
| `E_RECORD_STAT_NAME` | A RECORD block has an empty stat_name. |

## Example

The snippet seeds itself; its output is from a run made when this page was generated.

```python
from nagasim import build as nb

m = nb.Model(time_limit=100)
arrive = m.create(distribution=nb.Exponential(rate=1.0))
arrive >> m.record(stat_name="orders", kind="count") >> m.dispose()

results = m.run(seed=1)
print(results["user_summary"].to_string(index=False))
```

```text
 Run Statistic  Kind  Count  Value  Min  Max  Std
   1    orders count    100  100.0  NaN  NaN  NaN
```
